meta.title: Hire for an open role: requisition to signed contract

slides.title: Hire for an open role: requisition to signed contract
slides.subtitle: SOP-HR-002 · v1.0.0 · hr
slides.notes: Take an approved hiring need from an open requisition through sourcing, structured selection, a conditional offer, compliant screening, and a fully executed employment agreement — consistently, defensibly, and with the candidate experience and legal obligations handled at every step.

slides.title: Purpose & scope
bullets: Purpose: Take an approved hiring need from an open requisition through sourcing, structured selection, a conditional offer, compliant screening, and a fully executed employment agreement — consistently, defensibly, and with the candidate experience and legal obligations handled at every step.
In scope: Requisition creation and headcount/budget approval
In scope: Job description and job-related selection criteria
In scope: Sourcing, application screening, and interviews
In scope: Structured evaluation, selection, and reference checks
In scope: Conditional offer, FCRA-compliant background screening, and adverse action
In scope: Offer, negotiation, and execution of the employment agreement
In scope: Initiation of right-to-work (Form I-9) and handoff to onboarding
Out of scope: Day-one onboarding and orientation (see SOP-HR-001)
Out of scope: Long-range workforce planning and headcount strategy
Out of scope: Independent contractor / 1099 engagements
Out of scope: Immigration sponsorship and visa petitions
Outcome: A qualified candidate hired through a consistent, documented, defensible process
Outcome: A fully executed employment agreement on file
Outcome: Right-to-work verification initiated with a clean handoff to onboarding

slides.title: Roles
bullets: Hiring Manager: Owns the role, its requirements, and the final selection decision; Defines job-related criteria and participates in structured interviews
Recruiter / Talent Acquisition: Drives the process end to end and owns the candidate experience; Sources, screens, coordinates interviews, and extends offers
HR Business Partner: Oversees process compliance, recordkeeping, and offer/contract governance; Owns FCRA adverse action and right-to-work verification
Interview Panel: Conducts structured interviews and completes anchored scorecards; Provides evidence-based, job-related evaluations
Compensation / Finance Approver: Approves headcount, budget, and the compensation package; Confirms the offer sits within the approved band
Legal / Compliance: Reviews non-standard offer terms and the employment agreement; Advises on adverse action and jurisdictional requirements
Candidate: External party; responds to the offer and completes required documents

slides.title: Step 1: Open and document the requisition
bullets: Capture the confirmed hiring need as a requisition in the ATS: role, level, reporting line, justification, target start, and the business case. This is the record everything else hangs off.
$ ats req upsert --external-id "$REQ_KEY" --role "$ROLE_TITLE" --level "$LEVEL" --manager "$HM" --justification-file ./business-case.md

callouts.text: A requisition record exists in the ATS with role, level, reporting line, and business case.

slides.notes: Keep the business case job-related; it anchors the selection criteria.

slides.title: Step 2: Approve headcount and budget
bullets: Finance / compensation reviews the requisition against headcount plan and budget and either approves it to open or returns it. No sourcing happens before approval.

callouts.text: The requisition shows an approval record with approver, date, and budgeted band.

slides.title: Step 3: Finalize the job description and selection criteria
bullets: With the hiring manager, turn the requisition into an approved job description and a structured scorecard: 6–12 job-related competencies, each with behavioral anchors. Requirements must be necessary for the role.

callouts.text: Every listed requirement is job-related and consistent with business necessity; the scorecard defines competencies with behavioral anchors.

slides.title: Step 4: Source candidates
bullets: Post the role to the required internal and external channels and run sourcing and referrals to build a diverse, qualified pipeline. Honor any internal-posting or pay-transparency requirements.
$ ats job post --req "$REQ_ID" --channels internal,careers,linkedin --pay-range "$PAY_RANGE" --idempotency-key "$REQ_ID-post"

callouts.text: The role is posted to all required channels and a candidate pipeline is building in the ATS.

slides.notes: Include the pay range where pay-transparency law requires it.

slides.title: Step 5: Screen applications
bullets: Review applicants against the same job-related criteria and shortlist. Do not ask about criminal history at this stage where fair-chance law applies.
$ ats screen run --req "$REQ_ID" --criteria ./job-related-criteria.yaml --log ./screening-log.csv

callouts.text: All applicants are screened against the same criteria and screening decisions are logged.

slides.title: Step 6: Recruiter phone screen
bullets: Hold a consistent phone/video screen with each shortlisted candidate to confirm fit, motivation, logistics, and compensation expectations.

callouts.text: Each candidate is screened with the same core questions; notes are recorded in the ATS.

slides.title: Step 7: Administer job-related assessments
bullets: Where the role calls for it, administer the same validated, job-related assessment to every candidate and record results. Skip only if no assessment is used for this role.
$ ats assessment send --candidates ./shortlist.csv --assessment "$ASSESSMENT_ID" --if-not-sent

callouts.text: The same assessment is sent to all candidates for the role and results are recorded.

slides.title: Step 8: Conduct structured interviews
bullets: Run structured panel interviews using the same core questions for every candidate, scoring against the BARS scorecard. Offer reasonable accommodations on request.

callouts.text: Every interviewer completes an anchored scorecard with evidence notes; the same core questions were used.

slides.title: Step 9: Debrief and make the selection decision
bullets: Convene a structured debrief to reconcile scores against the anchors — not to reach consensus by social pressure — and make a documented, job-related decision. Retain the records.

callouts.text: The decision and its rationale are documented and stored; the selection-rate is checked against the 4/5 rule.

slides.title: Step 10: Complete reference checks
bullets: Run consistent, job-related reference checks on the selected candidate and record the results before making the offer conditional.

callouts.text: References are completed with consistent questions and results are recorded.

slides.title: Step 11: Approve compensation and extend a conditional verbal offer
bullets: Confirm the package is approved and within band, then extend a verbal offer that is explicitly conditional on clearing screening and right-to-work checks. Follow up in writing summarizing the key terms.

callouts.text: Compensation is approved and within band; the conditional verbal offer and its terms are confirmed by email.

slides.title: Step 12: Candidate response and negotiation
bullets: The candidate accepts, negotiates, or declines the conditional offer. Route accordingly; re-approve compensation for any counter-offer.

callouts.text: The candidate's response is recorded; any negotiated changes are captured before proceeding.

slides.title: Step 13: Disclose, authorize, and run the background check
bullets: Provide the standalone FCRA disclosure and obtain separate written authorization, then order the background check via the CRA. Keep the conditional offer in place while screening runs.
$ cra-api order --candidate "$CANDIDATE_ID" --package standard --auth-file ./signed-authorization.pdf --idempotency-key "$CANDIDATE_ID-$REQ_ID"

callouts.text: A signed standalone disclosure and authorization are on file before the report is ordered; the report is stored securely.

slides.title: Step 14: Adjudicate the results
bullets: Review the background and reference results. If nothing disqualifying is found, proceed to the written offer. If there is potentially disqualifying information, apply an individualized assessment and enter adverse action.

callouts.text: The adjudication applies job-relatedness and an individualized assessment; the rationale is documented.

slides.title: Step 15: Run FCRA adverse action (only if withdrawing)
bullets: Send the pre-adverse-action notice with a copy of the report and the Summary of Rights, wait a reasonable period for dispute (best practice at least five business days; some jurisdictions longer), then either restore the offer or send the final adverse-action notice.

callouts.text: Both notices are documented with dates and the waiting period is observed; no irreversible internal action is taken during the waiting period.

branches.condition: Dispute resolved in the candidate's favor or record corrected
Adverse action upheld — offer rescinded, revisit the shortlist

slides.title: Step 16: Extend the formal written offer
bullets: Issue the written offer letter / employment agreement matching the approved compensation and the verbal terms, with an acceptance deadline. Route any non-standard terms to Legal first.
$ esign send --template employment-agreement --candidate "$CANDIDATE_ID" --fields ./offer-terms.json --deadline "$ACCEPT_BY" --idempotency-key "$CANDIDATE_ID-offer"

callouts.text: The sent offer matches approved terms; non-standard terms were reviewed by Legal; an acceptance deadline is set.

slides.title: Step 17: Countersign and execute the agreement
bullets: On candidate signature, countersign to fully execute the employment agreement and confirm the start date. This is the signed contract that completes the hire.

callouts.text: Candidate signature and employer countersignature are on file; the start date is confirmed.

slides.title: Step 18: Initiate right-to-work and hand off to onboarding
bullets: Start Form I-9 and (if enrolled) E-Verify, and hand the new hire to onboarding. Section 1 is due no later than the first day; Section 2 within three business days of the start date.
$ everify case ensure --employee "$EMPLOYEE_ID" --start-date "$START_DATE"

callouts.text: Form I-9 is initiated and the onboarding handoff package is delivered to the onboarding owner.

slides.notes: I-9 Section 2 and day-one tasks complete in onboarding (SOP-HR-001).

slides.title: Safety & compliance
bullets: [compliance] Evaluate every candidate for the same role against the same job-related criteria, in the same order; do not discriminate on protected characteristics. (Title VII; ADEA; ADA)

[compliance] Interviews, tests, and screens are selection procedures — keep them job-related and consistent with business necessity, and monitor adverse impact (4/5 rule). (EEOC Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures (29 CFR Part 1607))

[data] Candidate and employee personal data must have a lawful basis, limited access, and defined retention; retain selection records at least one year (two years for federal contractors). (29 CFR 1602.14; GDPR / CCPA)

[compliance] A background check via a CRA requires a standalone written disclosure and separate authorization; an adverse decision requires the two-step FCRA process (pre-adverse notice with the report and a Summary of Rights, a reasonable waiting period, then a final adverse-action notice). (Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. 1681))

[compliance] Where fair-chance law applies, delay any criminal-history inquiry until after a conditional offer, and apply an EEOC individualized assessment (nature of the offense, time elapsed, job-relatedness). (Ban-the-box / fair-chance laws)

[legal] Verify employment eligibility with Form I-9 — Section 1 no later than the first day of work, Section 2 within three business days of the start date; run E-Verify if enrolled. (IRCA / Form I-9 (INA 274A))
[accessibility] Offer and honor reasonable accommodations to candidates with disabilities throughout the process. (ADA)
